'''Bernhard H. Korte''' (3 November 1938 – 26 April 2025) was a German computer scientist, a professor at the [[University of Bonn]] and an expert in [[combinatorial optimization]].

==Biography==
Korte earned his doctorate ([[Doctorate|Doctor rerum naturalium]]) from the University of Bonn in 1967. His thesis was entitled "Beiträge zur Theorie der Hardy'schen Funktionenklassen" (translated, "''Contributions to the theory of [[Hardy space|Hardy function classes]]''"), and was supervised by [[Ernst Peschl]] and Walter Thimm.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Bernhard Korte|id=46821}}.</ref> He earned his [[habilitation]] in 1971, and briefly held faculty positions at [[Regensburg University]] and [[Bielefeld University]] before joining the University of Bonn as a faculty member in 1972.<ref name="hcm">[http://www.hcm.uni-bonn.de/old/faculty//Korte/ Biography] at Hausdorff Center for Mathematics, University of Bonn, retrieved 18 July 2010.</ref> At the University of Bonn, Korte was the director of the Research Institute for [[Discrete Mathematics]].<ref>[http://www.or.uni-bonn.de/ Research Institute for Discrete Mathematics] at the University of Bonn, retrieved 18 July 2010.</ref>

Korte was a guest professor at [[Stanford University|Stanford]], [[Cornell University|Cornell]], the [[University of Waterloo]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], [[Yale University|Yale]] and [[Rutgers University]], along with institutions in [[Rome]], [[Pisa]], [[Barcelona]] and [[Rio de Janeiro]].

Korte died in [[Bonn]], [[North Rhine-Westphalia]] on 26 April 2025, at the age of 86.<ref>[https://www1.wdr.de/kultur/kulturnachrichten/universitaet-bonn-trauert-um-mathematiker-berhnard-korte100.amp Universität Bonn trauert um Mathematiker Bernhard Korte.] wdr.de, 30 April 2025 (in German). Retrieved 30 April 2025.</ref>

==Awards and honours==
In 1997, Korte received the State Prize of [[Nordrhein-Westfalen]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.geschichte.nrw.de/artikel.php?artikel%5Bid%5D=818&lkz=de |title=NRW Staatspreis für Korte |access-date=8 July 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120215215206/http://www.geschichte.nrw.de/artikel.php?artikel%5Bid%5D=818&lkz=de |archive-date=15 February 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and in 2002 he was awarded the Grand Cross of the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]]. He was also a winner of the [[Humboldt Prize]] and a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref name="hcm"/>
